confirmed: The husband identified in the marriage register.
read: «**+ Pietro De Franceschi di Giuseppe — Agricoltore**», witness 14 September 1818, signing with a cross. His brothers are **Cristoforo the weaver** and **Don Stefano the priest**, all «di Giuseppe» — so this household's father-in-law is a **Giuseppe De Franceschi**, alive in 1818.

confirmed: A burial found, and a grandfather named: 23 July 1829, house 48.
read: «**Pietro, figlio di Dom.co De Franceschi *q.m Pietro* e di Zacchera Cerlon di Franc.o**» — the death of a son names **Domenico's own dead father, a Pietro**. The baptism index gave this household as a bare pair of names; it now has a generation above it.

confirmed: Two burials found, and the husband written out three generations deep.
read: House **325**. Their daughter **Maria died 11 March 1829**; **Bonetta Vellico herself died 11 September 1830, aged 57**, of pulmonary consumption. Her entry names the husband as «**Stefano De Franceschi *di* Domenico *q.m* Pietro**» — father living, grandfather dead — which gives this household **three generations above it** where the baptism index gave none.

confirmed: Their marriage found: 9 June 1821, house 356, Vodnjan.
read: «**Gio: Maria De Franceschi figlio di Pietro De Franceschi q.m Gio: Maria e della fu Veniera Francin q.m Dom.co de Rondel**, giugali, Agricoltori», aged 22, marrying «**Lucia figlia di Giovanni Bonassin q.m Giuseppe e della fu Lucia Davanzo q.m Leonardo**», aged 27. The household gains a father, a grandfather and a great-grandfather in one line.

children.name: Pietro De Franceschi
children.note: Died aged 11 of scarlatina, house 456, without spiritual assistance because the illness was sudden.

confirmed: Their eldest son's death entry, 15 December 1830, names both parents with their patronymics.
read:
**15 December 1830, house 456.** «Pietro figlio di Pietro De Franceschi **q.m Pietro** e di Maddalena Francin **di Giovanni** giugali», aged **11** — born about **1819**, three years before the earliest baptism this archive had for the household, so **they were married by 1818**. Cause: **scarlatina**. In the sacraments column, «**senza assistenza spirituale per la malattia repentina**» — the same phrase the register used of Giuseppe De Franceschi q.m Pietro ten months earlier, and the second time this family loses somebody too fast for a priest.

The two patronymics are the point. The father is ***q.m* Pietro** — his own father was dead by 1830. The mother is ***di* Giovanni** — hers was alive. And the house is **456**, which is not 324 and not 325.

confirmed: Their marriage found: 25 January 1826, house 224, Vodnjan.
read: «**Fran.co figlio delli furono giugali Domenico Vellico q.m Andrea e Martina Biasiol**», aged 27, marrying «**Michiela figlia di Cristoforo De Franceschi q.m Gio: Maria e di Maria Luigia Manzin q.m Domenico**», aged 26. A household reconstructed from baptism entries, now **confirmed by the wedding that made it**, with both sets of parents named.

confirmed: Named in their daughter's second marriage, 25 June 1830.
read: «**Veniera, figlia delli furono giugali Gio. Maria De Franceschi *fu Pietro* e Michiela Zambaletta fu Cristoforo**». Neither parent appears in any baptism register on any film this archive can reach; the household exists **only** because a widow remarried at forty-nine and the clerk wrote her parents out in full. The dates are inferred from the children's stated ages.

confirmed: Named in their daughter's marriage, 19 November 1823.
read: «**Bonetta, figlia del fu Pietro De Franceschi q.m Dom.co e Domenica Manzin q.m Dom.co**», aged 23. A **second Vodnjan line**, unconnected to Giuseppe's sons and headed by a **Domenico**. The two sons are grouped here on the patronymic and the dates: both are «q.m Pietro» and both appear within months of Bonetta's wedding. *(inf)*

confirmed: Three daughters married out of the house, 1821, 1824 and 1825.
read: «**Lucia De Franceschi q.m Pietro**», wife of «Alvise Birattan q.m Saba». Her father Pietro was dead before 1821 and too old to be the Pietro who remarried in 1818 — so an **older Pietro again**. None of these three women appears in any index anywhere.

confirmed: Both parents named in their daughter's marriage, 27 July 1833; Giuseppe's death found, 14 February 1830.
read:
The household this archive circled for two days before it opened. **Giuseppe De Franceschi q.m Pietro** died at **house 324 on 14 February 1830, aged 72** — so born about **1758** — of an organic defect of the chest, and «*senza assistenza spirituale per morte improvvisa*», **suddenly and without a priest**. His wife **Lucia Tromba q.m Cristoforo** shares a surname with **Giovanni Tromba**, the parson who signs every page of these books and who licensed her son Don Stefano to baptise in 1816 and to marry couples in 1833.

Four children: **a priest, a ploughman, a weaver and a sister**. The two who worked with their hands signed the register with a cross.

read: **Pietro**, born about **1776**, of house 312; his first wife **Veniera Francin q.m Dom.co de Rondel** was dead by March 1818, when he remarried the widow Lorenza Tesser. The two sons' marriages name the couple identically nine years apart, which is what makes them one household. Pietro's father was the **Gio. Maria De Franceschi** who married Michiela Zambaletta.

read: **Cristoforo *q.m Gio: Maria*** — brother of the Pietro who remarried in 1818, and **not** the Cristoforo *di Giuseppe* who was a weaver. He is an **agricoltore**, and he stood as witness at his own niece's wedding in February 1828. Two men of one name in one town, told apart by the father's name and nothing else.

confirmed: Both named in their son's second marriage, 17 July 1832.
read: Both dead by 1832, when their son **Domenico**, forty-six and already a widower of Veniera De Rocchi, married again from **house 325** — the house of Stefano De Franceschi and Bonetta Vellico. **Which Pietro this is, the register does not say.**

confirmed: Four baptisms, 1817–1832, all naming the same couple.
read: A **De Franceschi daughter married out** into the Giachin house and stayed in Vodnjan. Her first child is born in **1817** and her last in **1832**, so she was married by 1816 and born around 1795 — which puts her a generation above the Stefano and Gio Maria households, not beside them. Two of her four children are given her own name, **Domenica** and **Michaela**. *Whose* daughter she was, the baptisms do not say.

confirmed: Four baptisms, 1848–1857. The index writes the mother twice as **Lucia** and twice as **Lucia Michaela**; the father is **Josephus Forlani** in all four.
read: A second daughter married out, thirty years after the first. Her four children run **1848–1857**, so she was born about 1825 — which is the right decade to be the **Lucia baptised 25 July 1826** to Gio Maria De Franceschi and Lucia Bonassin, or the **Lucia baptised 25 August 1828** to Pietro De Franceschi and Maddalena Francin. *inf* — two candidates, and nothing yet to choose between them.

confirmed: Two baptisms, 1858 and 1860.
read: A **Stefano De Franceschi** with a wife called **Maria Forlanichio**, whose two sons are **Giovanni Maria** and **Pietro** — the two names that run down the Vodnjan male line. A second Stefano is having children in the same parish in the same years by a **Maria Francin**. Either one man buried a wife and married again, or there are two Stefani. **The index cannot tell them apart, and neither can this archive yet** — the marriage register for the 1850s would settle it.

confirmed: Four baptisms, 1858–1865. The index spells the mother **Mathaea Delcarro** twice and **Mathea Delcaro** twice; the father is **Dominicus Defranceschi** in all four.
read: The eldest son is **Pietro**, the second **Stefano**, and the fourth is called **Venerius** — a boy given the feminine family name **Veniera** in its masculine form. Naming that hard is a household keeping a line in view. This Domenico is plausibly the **Domenico Giovanni Antonio baptised 1819** to Stefano De Franceschi and Bonetta Vellico of house 325, married about 1857 — *inf*, on the strength of the name, the parish and the arithmetic, and nothing more.

confirmed: Named in her daughter's death entry, 6 January 1831.
read:
**6 January 1831, house 24.** «Domenica figlia di **Andrea Palin q.m Pio.** e **della fu Michiela De Franceschi fu Pietro** giugali.»

Two deaths in one line. «*della fu*» puts the mother in the ground already; «*fu Pietro*» puts her father there too. So **Michiela De Franceschi, daughter of a Pietro, was dead before January 1831** — and this archive would never have heard of her at all if her daughter had not died young enough to need her named. A **sixth** woman who left the surname and came back only through a child.
